column2: North Sea Germanic nasalization of long a before a nasal
column8: Reformulated and split by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication: this rule now performs NASALIZATION only (*a-long > nasalized *a-long before a nasal); the rounding to *o-long is the separate later Anglo-Frisian change SC104. Earlier boundary: fed by SC024 (displacement of SC024 after this rule yields **manath, **spaan). Later boundary: it must precede SC004 EAFAiMonophthongization, demonstrated by displacing SC004 before this rule, which wrongly rounds the new *a-long < *ai (stone -> **ston, home -> **hom); *a-long < *ai arose only after nasalization (Campbell §132 pp.52-53; R/T pp.169-170). It feeds SC104: stating SC025 after SC104 strands the nasalized vowel and month and spoon are rejected.

Post-Proto-Germanic (Gothic bi-niuhsjan, saihsta retain the *h) and pre-breaking (R/T p.158: the undiphthongized vowels of waestm and thisl "can be accounted for only by supposing that these *h were lost before breaking took place"). R/T p.157 place it after the PWGmc *-CijV- syncope, which is what creates the *sj of *niuhsjan, so it is now composed immediately after PWGmcSyllabicJ. Fed by SC103 PGmcNasalLossBeforeX, which creates the *xst cluster of fist (*funxstiz > *fuxstiz); the two are separate historical changes, since Gothic underwent SC103 but not this one. Restaged out of the North Sea Germanic corridor, where it had wrongly followed the Ingvaeonic nasal-spirant law.

Reversal of the West Germanic gemination of *w before *j, restoring the diphthong: PNWGmc *awj > PWGmc *[aw'w'] > pre-OE *[auj] (R/T p.53 §3.1.3 'it was reversible'; Campbell §120.2 p.46 'auj > auuj > auj'). Feeds SC030, which then treats the new *au exactly like inherited *au (R/T p.173 'These new *au also underwent the development to éa').

Anglo-Frisian brightening applied to the first element of the diphthong *au, restricted to English. Campbell §132 p.52 groups 'West Gmc. a > OE æ; West Gmc. au > OE æu' in one ordered step; Fulk §4.12 p.73 makes it one fronting; R/T p.172 supply the *æu intermediate that CAPR encodes as *aeu. Scope is English, not Anglo-Frisian: OFris has ā with no fronting (OE ēac, ēage, bēam : OFris āk, āge, bām), and OE gēac has a palatalized initial where OFris gāk has none (Fulk §4.12 p.73; R/T p.172). Fed by SC029; feeds SC032, where R/T p.172's 'first tensed and fronted to æu ... later the offglide was unrounded and lowered' gives the historical direction.
